A little about my role

Not medical.
Just there,
for you.

A doula is a trained birth companion. I do not replace your midwife or doctor. I am the familiar person who knows your wishes, keeps the room calm and reminds you to drink water.

Before the birth we talk through your options, your fears and your plan. During labour I stay with you for as long as you need me, at home or in hospital.

Afterwards I visit to help with feeding, rest and the many small questions nobody warns you about.

One step at a time

No need to have
it all figured out.

We start with a conversation.
And take it from there.

  1. A free first call.

    Twenty minutes to see if we get on. No pressure, no sales pitch.

  2. Getting to know you.

    Two visits at home to talk about your wishes, your partner's role and what helps you feel safe.

  3. The birth.

    From 38 weeks I am on call day and night. When you need me, I come and I stay.

  4. After the birth.

    I visit in the first week and we talk through how it went, at your pace.

A few things you might be wondering

There are no silly questions.

When should I book?

Most families book in the second trimester, but I am happy to talk at any stage.

Do you attend hospital births?

Yes. The example practice covers Southmead, St Michael's and home births across Bristol.

Can my partner still be involved?

Of course. Part of my job is helping your partner feel useful and confident.

What if you are ill when I go into labour?

The example arrangement is a trusted backup doula you would meet before the birth. Confirm this directly with any real provider.

Can I pay in instalments?

The example fee can be split into three payments before your due date. No payments are taken here.
